mitigation_descriptions: Setting the timestamp_timeout to 0 will require the user to input their password every time sudo is executed. Similarly, ensuring that the tty_tickets setting is enabled will prevent this leakage across tty sessions.

The sudoers file should be strictly edited such that passwords are always required and that users can’t spawn risky processes as users with higher privilege. By requiring a password, even if an adversary can get terminal access, they must know the password to run anything in the sudoers file.
reasoning: The adversary activity was confirmed for technique T1548.003 involving unauthorized sudo executions to root by user phopkins on intranet-server.
remediation_plan: 1. Isolate the affected host intranet-server (10.35.35.206) and revoke active sessions for user phopkins. 2. Edit the sudoers configuration to strictly require passwords for all executions and prevent spawning higher-privilege processes. 3. Set timestamp_timeout to 0 in sudoers to mandate password re-entry on every sudo execution. 4. Enable the tty_tickets setting to prevent sudo credential leakage across terminal sessions.
